description: Behavioral exercises: the coach sets a concrete task and grades the SUBMITTED ARTIFACT (code), not a self-report. Objective `checks` (regex over the submission) give a keyless, deterministic signal; the code-reading rubric judge integrates them. Keyed by competency_id from competency_map.json.

exercises.title: Resilient batch of LLM calls
exercises.prompt: Write an async function `run_batch(prompts, call_llm)` that runs ~500 LLM calls concurrently but safely: cap concurrency, retry transient failures with backoff, apply a per-call timeout, and return results without letting one failure sink the batch.
exercises.rubric: L4 code: async with an explicit concurrency cap (Semaphore), retry with backoff, per-call timeout (wait_for), and it isolates per-call failures. L2: a plain loop or unbounded gather with no limits/retries/timeouts.

exercises.title: Schema-valid JSON with recovery
exercises.prompt: Write `get_person(text, call_llm)` that returns a validated object with fields name:str and age:int from the model. Use a schema, validate the output, and recover (retry) on invalid output instead of trusting raw text.
exercises.rubric: L4: typed schema (Pydantic/JSON schema / structured-output mode), explicit validation, and a retry that feeds the error back. L2: json.loads on free text with no validation or recovery.

exercises.title: Structure-aware chunker
exercises.prompt: Write `chunk_document(text)` for legal contracts. Don't just cut every N characters: respect structure (sections/paragraphs), use overlap, and attach metadata to each chunk.
exercises.rubric: L4: splits on structural boundaries, configurable overlap, per-chunk metadata, reasons about size. L2: fixed-size slicing with no overlap/structure.

checks.description: Splits on structure, not just fixed size

exercises.title: Bound a runaway agent loop
exercises.prompt: Here is an agent loop that can spin forever and blindly trusts tool calls. Rewrite `run_agent(task, tools)` to be reliable: cap the steps, validate tool selection/args, handle tool errors, and terminate cleanly.
exercises.rubric: L4: explicit step limit, validated tool dispatch, error handling/fallback, clear termination. L2: unbounded while loop, no validation or guards.

exercises.title: Harden a doc-reading tool
exercises.prompt: Write `handle_document(user_doc, run_tool)` where the document is UNTRUSTED and the agent can call tools. Defend against prompt injection: isolate untrusted content, restrict which tools/args are allowed, and never execute instructions from the document.
exercises.rubric: L4: treats content as data (delimiters/separate channel), tool allow-list with arg checks, no execution of doc-derived commands. L2: concatenates the doc into the prompt and trusts it.
